commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-55077: Fix RiskAssessment method example ValueSet link
commits.summary: Completed the Applied FHIR-55077 RiskAssessment terminology update by fixing the method example CodeSystem's stale ValueSet canonical.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-55077 required the RiskAssessment method and outcome terminology artifacts to become experimental Example artifacts, and this commit fixes the remaining method CodeSystem link that still pointed at the old non-Example ValueSet canonical.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55077 was Applied/Persuasive and specifically resolved to mark the RiskAssessment method and outcome ValueSets and CodeSystems experimental and add Example to each id, url, name, and title. The current method CodeSystem source had already been renamed to the Example artifact, but its CodeSystem.valueSet still referenced http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/risk-assessment-method instead of the renamed http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/risk-assessment-method-example. Because CodeSystem.valueSet is part of the published terminology/conformance metadata, the stale canonical would leave the renamed CodeSystem pointing to an obsolete non-Example ValueSet. Updating this one canonical is required to complete the Jira-directed artifact rename, not adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an authoritative RiskAssessment CodeSystem XML source, so the valueSet canonical is emitted in the current terminology/conformance artifact. Leaving it stale would publish a method Example CodeSystem whose metadata points to the pre-rename method ValueSet while the active method ValueSet and RiskAssessment bindings use the Example canonical.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix completing FHIR-55077's terminology rename; no separate WG path is needed for this narrow canonical alignment.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution required the RiskAssessment method and outcome ValueSets and CodeSystems to be experimental Example artifacts, including Example in their ids and urls. That directly requires the method CodeSystem.valueSet metadata to reference the renamed Example method ValueSet canonical rather than the previous non-Example canonical.

caveats: This assessment is limited to the single changed CodeSystem source file; the related method ValueSet and RiskAssessment bindings already use the Example canonical.

triage.fhir_spec_impact: The Procedure StructureDefinition XML is authoritative conformance source, so the stale comment affects current rendered element guidance and distributed StructureDefinition content. triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the change as a Jira-backed editorial correction for FHIR-55327. Review the StructureDefinition hunk as the primary authoritative fix and the event-mapping exception hunk as synchronized Procedure.status wording for the same resolved contraction.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-55973: Require distinct repeated Questionnaire answers
commits.summary: Updated active Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse source so repeated question answers must be distinct.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-55973 explicitly resolved that repeated Questionnaire answers must be distinct and that QuestionnaireResponse should prohibit duplicate answers for the same question. The commit updates only the active Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse StructureDefinition sources needed to reflect that decision.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55973 was Applied/Persuasive and its resolution specifically required adding a QuestionnaireResponse.item invariant with the human text "The same answer cannot be specified more than once for the same question", changing Questionnaire.item.repeats definition/comment wording from multiple answers to multiple distinct answers, and moving the group/question representation note to the start of the repeats comment. Before this commit, the active source still had the older non-distinct Questionnaire.item.repeats wording and QuestionnaireResponse.item lacked the qrs-4 duplicate-answer invariant and answer condition reference. These StructureDefinition XML files are authoritative current-build inputs for rendered resource definitions, generated conformance resources, and validation constraints. The proposed edits are the concrete source changes named by the Jira resolution, not adjacent cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The Questionnaire edit changes reader-visible definition/comment text for Questionnaire.item.repeats. The QuestionnaireResponse edit adds an error-level invariant and condition reference, affecting generated conformance artifacts and validation behavior for repeated answer values.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed fix for FHIR-55973; no alternate attribution, subset filtering, or new WG path is needed for these source changes.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution explicitly required distinct-answer wording in Questionnaire.item.repeats and a QuestionnaireResponse.item invariant prohibiting the same answer more than once for the same question. The commit implements those requirements in the active StructureDefinition sources.

caveats: The invariant expression is implemented as answer.value.isDistinct().allTrue(), which is semantically aligned with the Jira-requested answer.value.isDistinct() duplicate-answer rule.

caveats: Public build checks showed the introduction typo on paymentreconciliation.html and the PaymentReconciliation.kind typo in rendered/generated StructureDefinition content.
Searches of paymentreconciliation-mappings.html, profile XML/JSON, and available QA pages did not establish current output impact for the mapping-exception "occurence" text.

If maintainers know the mapping-exception file feeds an unpublished but required QA artifact, that hunk can be accepted as consistent cleanup, but it should not be the basis for treating the entire commit as a Jira-backed missed application.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-55634: Align lastVersionPresent CRMI reference
commits.summary: Updated the FHIR-core lastVersionPresent concept property definition and narrative table to reference the final CRMI includeNoLongerPresent parameter name.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: the FHIR-core lastVersionPresent concept property text was left pointing at the obsolete CRMI ValueSet/$expand parameter name. The core issue provides the property context, but the final parameter-name decision is better attributed to FHIR-55634.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-56201 resolved that the core concept-properties CodeSystem should define lastVersionPresent and include it in the defined concept-properties table, while the linked FHIR-55634 resolution finalized the CRMI ValueSet/$expand parameter as includeNoLongerPresent and stated that returned expansion concepts SHOULD carry the lastVersionPresent concept property. The missed application is that the active core CodeSystem definition and the reader-visible defined-properties table still referenced includeLastVersionPresent, an earlier parameter name no longer matching the CRMI decision. Because those two files publish the CodeSystem definition and narrative table for the current spec, the stale cross-reference would direct implementers to the wrong CRMI parameter. Updating both occurrences to includeNoLongerPresent is the narrow required completion of the linked Jira decisions, not optional cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/codesystem/codesystem-concept-properties.xml is authoritative CodeSystem source for the concept property definition, and source/codesystem/codesystem-notes.xml supplies the rendered defined concept-properties table. The change corrects current conformance/narrative text by replacing a stale CRMI parameter cross-reference with the applied parameter name; it does not change the property code, datatype, or expansion semantics.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the change as a Jira-backed correction, and cite FHIR-55634 alongside FHIR-56201 so the final includeNoLongerPresent parameter decision is visible in the review history.

jira_evidence.explanation: This Applied/Persuasive with Modification CRMI issue resolved the ValueSet/$expand input parameter as includeNoLongerPresent and says returned concepts SHOULD have the lastVersionPresent concept property. That final parameter decision directly determines the correct target of the FHIR-core cross-reference.

This Applied/Persuasive with Modification core issue required adding lastVersionPresent as a string concept property and adding it to the defined concept-properties table. It explains why the property belongs in core, but its own resolution text used the intermediate includeLastVersionPresent parameter name.

caveats: The change is limited to the cross-reference text in active CodeSystem and narrative source; it does not alter the lastVersionPresent concept code, datatype, or behavior.
The shown issue key is only partial attribution because FHIR-55634 is the decision that finalized includeNoLongerPresent.

commits.summary: Fixed the applied ImagingStudy numberOfFrames change so active source surfaces consistently describe ImagingStudy.series.instance.numberOfFrames.

FHIR-55483 approved adding the element for DICOM Number Of Frames, and the current XML source still had incorrect element text, mapping punctuation, and a non-existent plural path in reader-facing narrative.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55483 was resolved Applied/Persuasive for R6 to add ImagingStudy.series.instance.numberOfFrames as a 0..1 unsignedInt for the DICOM Number Of Frames (0028,0008) value in multiframe instances. The current StructureDefinition had the element but still described it as the instance ordinal, retained a malformed definition and DICOM tag spelling, and the ImagingStudy introduction referred to the non-existent path ImagingStudy.series.instances.numberOfFrames. Those surfaces affect the rendered element details, generated conformance artifact text/mapping, and rendered ImagingStudy narrative. The edits are required to finish applying the approved element's intended meaning and path, not merely to tidy adjacent files.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/imagingstudy/structuredefinition-ImagingStudy.xml is the authoritative conformance source for ImagingStudy element definitions and mappings, so the stale short, definition, and DICOM mapping affect generated StructureDefinition content and rendered detailed descriptions. source/imagingstudy/imagingstudy-introduction.xml is rendered narrative, so the plural instances path would point readers at a path that does not exist.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep these XML source corrections as the FHIR-55483 application fix.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue requested and approved adding ImagingStudy.series.instance.numberOfFrames to carry the number of frames in a multiframe image, with unsignedInt cardinality 0..1 and DICOM mapping to Number Of Frames (0028,0008). That decision directly requires the active StructureDefinition and narrative to use the singular instance path and to describe frame count rather than an instance ordinal.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider a consistency check that flags narrative references to non-existent element paths and DICOM mapping values with malformed tag punctuation.
caveats: The approved Jira XML snippet itself appears to have copied the short text from ImagingStudy.series.instance.number, but the issue title, description, element path, alias, type, and DICOM mapping all identify this as a frame-count element.
This commit contains only the StructureDefinition and introduction XML changes; it does not require treating any layout-only SVG hunk as part of the Jira-backed fix.

The structural change was already present, but source/datatypes/dosage.xml still had adjacent requirements/comment text saying the site was a coded specification and that BodyStructure-like detail should use the bodySite extension, which conflicts with the new CodeableReference capability. Updating those two cells is required to complete the Jira application because it removes guidance that contradicts the specific adopted type change while preserving the existing coded binding.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/datatypes/dosage.xml is the active source for the Dosage datatype; its element definitions, requirements, and comments feed current rendered Dosage documentation and conformance-facing guidance. caveats: The commit only touches source/datatypes/dosage.xml; it does not mix in generated, derived, or diagram collateral.
The duplicate issue context is supporting only; FHIR-54848 itself is sufficient to justify this narrow Dosage.site guidance change.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

commits.summary: Completed the applied AdverseEvent.actuality unknown-code change by updating the build-scoped AdverseEvent-actuality SearchParameter description.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: Patient Care resolved to add an unknown value for AdverseEvent.actuality, but the active AdverseEvent actuality SearchParameter still described the token values as only actual and potential. Updating that description keeps the SearchParameter artifact aligned with the required-bound code set.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55315 was resolved as Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 and specifically required adding an unknown code to the AdverseEvent.actuality code system and value set, with the definition that the source system does not specify which current value applies and with discouraging legacy-data guidance. The terminology and element metadata had already been updated, but source/adverseevent/bundle-AdverseEvent-search-params.xml still described the AdverseEvent.actuality token search as only "actual | potential". Because that SearchParameter is the conformance source for searches over AdverseEvent.actuality, the stale enumeration omitted a Jira-required allowed code from current artifact-facing and reader-facing search documentation. The proposed one-line edit is required to complete the Jira application on this search surface, rather than being optional consistency cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the AdverseEvent SearchParameter bundle, an authoritative source for current search parameter conformance/rendered content. The edit does not change the search expression or validation behavior, but it corrects the SearchParameter description so it no longer contradicts the AdverseEvent.actuality code system, value set, and element short text that now include unknown.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a narrow Jira-backed completion of the AdverseEvent.actuality unknown-code change.

jira_evidence.explanation: Patient Care resolved the issue as Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6, requiring an unknown code for AdverseEvent.actuality with the definition that the source system does not specify which current value applies, plus a comment that the code is for legacy data and strongly discouraged. Once that code is present in the required-bound actuality value set, the SearchParameter description listing only actual and potential is stale and misleading for the same search surface.

Earlier discussion considered a boolean or two-value model, but the later Patient Care resolution chose the compatible unknown-code approach; no superseding reversal was identified in the provided evidence.

caveats: Search parameter descriptions can legitimately differ from element definitions, but this one is an explicit pipe-separated list of actuality token values; after FHIR-55315, omitting unknown incorrectly suggests that token is not part of the search surface.
The commit touches only editor-owned XML for the AdverseEvent SearchParameter bundle and no generated, derived, or hard-avoid files.

commits.summary: Completed the Applied FHIR-48399 Patient.multipleBirth[x] clarification by updating the active core short display to include pre-birth/potential multiple-birth use.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-48399 explicitly approved changing the Patient.multipleBirth[x] short display to include potential pre-birth multiple-birth use. This commit updates the active Patient StructureDefinition source to the approved short display.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-48399 was Applied/Persuasive by Patient Administration and its resolution specifically required Patient.multipleBirth[x] to use the short display "Whether patient is part or potentially part of a multiple birth", along with definition and comment wording clarifying known multiple fetuses before birth and limiting valueInteger to after live birth. The current core Patient StructureDefinition had already received the approved definition and comments, but still retained the old short display "Whether patient is part of a multiple birth", leaving a concrete part of the approved resolution unapplied. Because this StructureDefinition is the authoritative core Patient conformance source and the element short display is generated into rendered definitions and conformance metadata, the omission affects current spec output. The proposed one-line edit is required to complete the approved Patient.multipleBirth[x] wording, rather than being adjacent cleanup or optional consistency work.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/patient/structuredefinition-Patient.xml is the authoritative Patient StructureDefinition input. Patient.multipleBirth[x].short appears in the rendered element definitions and generated conformance artifact metadata, so the old wording omits the approved pre-birth/potential multiple-birth clarification from current specification output.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-48399. The commit changes only the missing core Patient short display; the related patient-multipleBirthTotal extension text is maintained outside core and is reported as already updated.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive resolution explicitly says the Patient.multipleBirth[x] short display will be "Whether patient is part or potentially part of a multiple birth" and also clarifies pre-birth fetus use in the definition and comments. The commit changes the remaining core short display to that approved text.
The related discussion appears to have led to FHIR-48399, but the broader issue is not needed to justify this edit because FHIR-48399 contains the concrete approved Patient.multipleBirth[x] wording.

caveats: This assessment relies on the Patient StructureDefinition short display being generated into rendered definitions and conformance metadata, not merely on the file being listed in build scope.
No SVG, generated model-definition, or other editor-avoided file is part of this commit.

This commit fixes the remaining operation definition and request example surfaces that still described a MeasureReport input, an instance-level request URL, or the obsolete MeasureReport.patient element.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-50487 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and specifically resolved to make the R6 Measure $submit-data operation identical to the DEQM STU 5 operation, with URL [base]/Measure/$submit-data, no Measure instance invocation, and an operation example updated to submit a Bundle. The current source missed that application because the input parameter was named/documented as a bundle with max="*" but still typed as MeasureReport, the request example still used [base]/Measure/Measure-mrp/$submit-data despite the type-level-only decision, and the submitted MeasureReport inside the required Bundle example still used patient rather than the current subject element. These files feed the current Measure operation definition and operation-page examples, so the mismatch affects formal conformance/source example correctness. The proposed edits are necessary to complete the approved DEQM alignment rather than optional cleanup because they change the formal parameter type and the exact example invocation/content that the resolution required to be Bundle-based and type-level.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The OperationDefinition XML is authoritative conformance source for Measure $submit-data and determines the formal input parameter type. The request text and JSON are the operation example sources, so the URL and embedded MeasureReport element name affect current reader-visible example correctness rather than only repository hygiene.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-50487; no new issue or WG path is needed for these three editor-owned source updates.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution says to make the R6 Measure $submit-data operation identical to the DEQM STU 5 operation, gives the URL as [base]/Measure/$submit-data, states the operation is not allowed on a Measure instance because the MeasureReport in the Bundle specifies the measure, and says the operation example must be updated to submit a Bundle. That directly requires the Bundle parameter type and type-level request example, and supports correcting the Bundle example content to use the current MeasureReport.subject element.

This adjacent Applied/Persuasive Measure operation alignment issue uses the same DEQM multi-cardinality Bundle pattern for $collect-data. It supports consistency across the Measure operation family but is not the primary authority for the $submit-data edit.

caveats: The direct authority is FHIR-50487 and the DEQM STU 5 operation shape it explicitly incorporates.
The MeasureReport.subject change is part of the same required Bundle request example update, not a separate generated-file or hard-avoid-file cleanup.

triage.category_rationale: FHIR-47622 was an Applied/Persuasive R6 Pharmacy decision requiring the current Medication.batch BackboneElement to be renamed to Medication.instance, adding Medication.instance.identifier 0..* Identifier for the physical instance, typically a serial number, and ensuring serial numbers are not represented through the general Medication.identifier concept. The base source still missed that application in concrete current surfaces: Medication.identifier still commented that a serial number could be included there, the serial-number SearchParameter still queried Medication.identifier and had a stale path/description, the lot-number SearchParameter path still named Medication.batch.lotNumber, and several active contained Medication examples still used the removed batch element. The StructureDefinition and SearchParameter bundle are authoritative build inputs, so those stale entries affect rendered conformance/search-parameter content and search semantics; the example files are editor-owned example source tied to current example pages and should conform to the renamed Medication model. The proposed edits are required to complete the same Jira application because they redirect the serial-number behavior to the newly added instance.identifier element and replace the old batch path/name where it remained, rather than making an optional later terminology or style cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/medication/structuredefinition-Medication.xml affects rendered Medication element documentation and conformance artifacts, and source/medication/bundle-Medication-search-params.xml affects the current Medication SearchParameter definitions and expressions. The contained Medication example files are active source examples, not generated or hard-avoid files; their batch-to-instance renames keep example content consistent with the current Medication structure, though the strongest current-spec impact comes from the authoritative StructureDefinition and SearchParameter corrections.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as the FHIR-47622 follow-through fix. Reviewers should preserve the StructureDefinition and SearchParameter changes as required, and keep the contained-example tag renames as matching cleanup for the same backbone rename unless separate build evidence shows those source example elements are never emitted or validated.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution specifically requires renaming Medication.batch to Medication.instance, adding Medication.instance.identifier for physical-instance identifiers such as serial numbers, and avoiding serial-number use in the general Medication.identifier concept. That directly requires the Medication.identifier comment and serial-number SearchParameter to stop pointing at Medication.identifier, requires lot-number paths to use Medication.instance rather than Medication.batch, and supports updating active Medication examples that still use the removed batch element.

triage.tooling_recommendation: If the publisher silently strips or ignores removed elements in example source, add a QA warning so stale example XML is visible instead of being hidden as source-tree debt.
caveats: No hard-avoid generated files or SVG/layout files are changed.
The remaining Medication.batch references in fhir.ini are compatibility aliases and are not part of this source correction.

The contained example changes are tied to the same backbone rename, but proof of generated-output survival for the old batch element was not available; the decisive current conformance impact is in the StructureDefinition and SearchParameter inputs.

triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an authoritative datatype source, not a generated-only artifact. These spreadsheet cells affect current rendered SampledData descriptive text, conformance element short/definition content for intervalUnit, and the human-readable invariant text associated with the interval/offsets constraint.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-35948. No separate attribution, subset application, or new WG path is needed for this narrow wording alignment.

commits.subject: FHIR-47677: Fix Appointment is-recurring search expression
commits.summary: Corrected the Appointment is-recurring search parameter so it uses logical OR for the approved recurrence-template-or-originating-appointment semantics.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-47677 approved an Appointment is-recurring token search parameter whose semantics are true when the Appointment has a recurrence template or an originating appointment. The existing SearchParameter used the FHIRPath union operator between two boolean exists() results, so changing it to logical or is required to match the approved recurrence-search behavior.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-47677 was resolved Applied/Persuasive with Modification and specifically required new Appointment recurrence-series search parameters, including is-recurring as a token parameter for "has template OR has originating appointment". The current authoritative Appointment search-parameter bundle contains that parameter, but the expression was `Appointment.recurrenceTemplate.exists() | Appointment.originatingAppointment.exists()`, which does not encode the approved boolean disjunction. Because this bundle generates the current Appointment SearchParameter conformance artifact, the stale expression affects the published search definition rather than just source cleanliness. The proposed edit is the narrow correction needed to complete the Jira application: it changes only the expression to `Appointment.recurrenceTemplate.exists() or Appointment.originatingAppointment.exists()` and does not add adjacent cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative source for Appointment search parameters. Its expression is carried into the generated SearchParameter conformance resource and defines the current search behavior for is-recurring; the old expression did not faithfully represent the Jira-approved has-template-or-has-originating-appointment semantics.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the change as the Jira-backed fix for FHIR-47677. No additional attribution, rollup issue, or WG path appears necessary for this narrow expression correction.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution expressly approved Appointment recurrence-series search support and listed is-recurring as a token search parameter with "has template OR has originating appointment" semantics, directly requiring a boolean OR expression over recurrenceTemplate.exists() and originatingAppointment.exists().

caveats: This assessment treats source/appointment/bundle-Appointment-search-params.xml as the editor-owned source for the generated Appointment SearchParameter artifacts.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-51607: Link published compartment extension
commits.summary: Removed stale unpublished-extension wording from the active StructureDefinition additional-resource narrative and linked to the published additional-resource-compartment extension.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-51607 accepted the additional-resource-compartment StructureDefinition extension mechanism for documenting compartment membership of additional resources, and the active StructureDefinition narrative still said that extension was not yet published. This commit removes the stale publication caveat and links the now-published extension.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-51607 specifically resolved to define a repeatable additionalResourceCompartment extension on StructureDefinition, with components for compartment, membership parameters, documentation, and $everything start/end parameters, to document how post-R6 additional resources participate in compartments. The current additional-resource rules in source/structuredefinition/structuredefinition-notes.xml already point to that mechanism but still describe the extension as "yet to be published"; that is the missed application, because the accepted mechanism is now a published extension rather than future work. This narrative is active StructureDefinition documentation, so the stale qualifier affects reader-visible current guidance for additional-resource definitions. Replacing the qualifier with a link to the canonical extension is required to complete the Jira-backed documentation path, rather than being optional consistency cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is active StructureDefinition narrative source and affects rendered explanatory text for additional-resource StructureDefinitions. It does not change conformance cardinalities or CompartmentDefinition instances, but it corrects reader-visible guidance and the canonical reference for documenting compartment membership of additional resources.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed narrative correction for FHIR-51607. Do not expand this into CompartmentDefinition instance edits; any future refinements to extension details should be handled in the extension/tooling source that publishes additional-resource-compartment.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution required defining an additionalResourceCompartment extension on StructureDefinition to document compartment membership determinations for additional resources, including compartment, param, documentation, startParam, and endParam components. The edited StructureDefinition narrative is the core documentation surface for those additional-resource rules and still described the accepted extension as unpublished.

This issue clarified that HL7-defined CompartmentDefinition instances are not a computable mechanism for a server's additional or reduced compartment implementation. That supports using the StructureDefinition extension mechanism rather than changing core CompartmentDefinition instances.

caveats: The correction depends on the accepted extension mechanism now being published; the Jira resolution established the mechanism, and the current publication state makes the old qualifier stale.
The commit changes only editor-owned narrative source and does not include generated, derived, or hard-avoid files.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

commits.summary: Clarified MedicationAdministration subpotent descriptions so the element and its reason consistently refer to the full ordered dose.

This commit completes that clarification in the authoritative MedicationAdministration resource definition.

The original application updated only MedicationAdministration.isSubPotent.short, leaving isSubPotent.definition and the closely coupled subPotentReason short/definition with the same ambiguous full dose phrasing that the WG addressed. These strings are active StructureDefinition element descriptions, so they affect implementer-facing rendered documentation and generated conformance artifacts. Replacing the remaining full-dose wording with full ordered dose is required to finish the Jira application rather than being optional consistency cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the active MedicationAdministration StructureDefinition source. Its element short and definition text feed current rendered resource documentation and conformance-facing StructureDefinition content, so the stale wording could continue to imply a typical/usual full dose rather than the ordered dose.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed fix for FHIR-46911. No subset should be dropped; the commit only changes editor-owned authoritative source and does not include generated or layout-only collateral.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue identified MedicationAdministration.isSubPotent's 'Full dose was not administered' description as confusing and explicitly noted that the concern also reflected on subPotentReason. The resolution kept the subPotent term but required the description to say 'An indication that the full ordered dose was not administered'.

The Pharmacy WG minutes record that 'full dose' was ambiguous between the intended full ordered dose and a typical or usual guideline dose, and that the motion to add 'ordered' passed. That supports applying the ordered-dose clarification consistently to the definition and the reason element tied to the same concept.

caveats: The resolution's quoted replacement sentence names the isSubPotent description directly; the subPotentReason updates are justified because the Jira description explicitly called out that related element and because its text explains the same full-ordered-dose condition.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the ImagingStudy narrative notes source, which contributes reader-visible rendered specification text. The stale example would instruct readers to place identifier under a non-existent wrapper inside basedOn, while the resource definition and search parameters already reflect the basedOn/Reference.identifier model.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source fix as a Jira-backed correction, but cite FHIR-41484 for the exact wrapper-removal requirement and FHIR-49675 only as supporting context for the current basedOn/Reference.identifier model.

jira_evidence.explanation: This Applied/Persuasive technical correction is titled "The accession number example mistakenly holds a \"reference\" level" and its resolution says to update the build.fhir.org ImagingStudy notes Accession Number encoding example as described. triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider a QA check that parses JSON snippets in rendered narrative examples where feasible, because this was a reader-visible example-shape error rather than a conformance-source defect.
caveats: No StructureDefinition or search-parameter source change is implicated by this commit; those sources already implement the basedOn/Reference.identifier model.
The shown issue explains why the accession example belongs under basedOn, but the exact one-line deletion is better attributed to FHIR-41484.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-39432: Align DeviceMetric model metadata

The missed current source surface is source/library/library-fhir-helpers-content.cql, which still declared helper overloads for FHIR.DeviceMetricCategory and FHIR.DeviceMetricCalibrationType even though those wrapper model types are no longer the approved representation of the DeviceMetric elements. That CQL file is referenced as the content of the active FHIRHelpers Library, so the stale overloads affect published Library/CQL content rather than only source-tree cleanliness. Removing these two overloads is required to finish aligning the helper library with the approved datatype change; it is not a separate terminology migration or optional wording cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The patch affects current Library/CQL content: source/library/library-fhir-helpers.xml points its text/cql content at library-fhir-helpers-content.cql, and the FHIRHelpers Library is listed among Library examples. triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the CQL helper removal as the Jira-backed source fix, but pair it with regeneration or consistency checking for the model-definition artifacts instead of hand-editing the generated XML files.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution explicitly changed DeviceMetric.category and DeviceMetric.calibration.type to CodeableConcept with extensible bindings. Helper overloads for DeviceMetricCategory and DeviceMetricCalibrationType are stale collateral from the old required-code model and should not remain in the published FHIRHelpers CQL Library once that decision is applied.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Add a generator or consistency check that compares FHIRHelpers overloads and model-definition conversion metadata against the authoritative StructureDefinitions, and regenerate model-definition artifacts when datatype changes remove code-wrapper model types.
caveats: The generated/derived model-definition files still contain DeviceMetricCategory and DeviceMetricCalibrationType references in this commit context; those files are hard-avoid editor surfaces and should be regenerated or handled separately rather than hand-edited.

Applying only this CQL deletion without a corresponding generated-artifact update may leave stale conversionInfo/typeInfo in model-definition XML, so reviewers should treat the generated-artifact synchronization as a follow-on regeneration requirement rather than restoring the obsolete helper overloads.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-17075: Align history entry requirements
commits.summary: Reconciled the stale HTTP history paragraph left by the 2015 transaction-relaxation issue with later current-spec rules that require request and response details for history entries.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application in the reader-visible HTTP history narrative, but the current rule is better attributed to FHIR-17075 and FHIR-38942 than to FHIR-7933 alone. The edit removes stale text that made request details appear optional for history entries even though current Bundle rules require request and response details.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-17075 required the specification to make clear that history Bundles have response information for each entry and identified the missing request requirement; FHIR-38942 later confirmed that the Bundle entry requirements belong in current invariants. The existing HTTP history paragraph still said each entry could minimally contain either a resource or request details, and the request sentence was incomplete, so the active narrative conflicted with the current history conformance rule requiring request and response. Because source/http.html is rendered HTTP guidance, the mismatch was visible to readers and could misstate what history entries must contain. Updating that paragraph to require request and response, while preserving the PUT/POST resource rule and non-REST-equivalent request explanation, is necessary to complete the later history Bundle rule in narrative rather than being optional cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/http.html is rendered as current HTTP interaction guidance. Before this change, its history section could be read as permitting history entries with only a resource and no request, contradicting the current Bundle history invariant requiring request and response; the update aligns narrative guidance with existing conformance behavior.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source change as a Jira-backed fix, but attribute the current request/response requirement primarily to FHIR-17075 with FHIR-38942 as supporting context; treat FHIR-7933 as historical context for why the stale optional-request wording existed.

jira_evidence.explanation: This Published/Persuasive issue specifically asked whether request and response are mandatory for history and resolved to make the history Bundle response requirement clear, with discussion identifying the need for a request constraint. That directly supports replacing optional-request HTTP wording with text requiring request and response details.

This Published/Persuasive issue moved Bundle entry SHALL requirements into invariants while leaving other explanatory language. The current Bundle invariant requiring request and response for history entries shows that the conformance rule the HTTP narrative must align with is deliberate current source.

This older Published/Persuasive with Modification issue removed the old requirement that every history entry contain a transaction because versions can be created outside REST interactions. It explains the historical origin of the stale resource-or-request wording, but it does not by itself justify today's mandatory request/response wording.

This Published/Persuasive issue clarified that PATCH-created history entries are represented as PUT and added the prohibition on PATCH as a history request method. It supports not expanding this HTTP paragraph to say PATCH request methods are allowed in history.

This later Published issue said to include PATCH in the history resource rule, but that conflicts with the current PATCH prohibition for history request methods. It should be handled separately rather than as the basis for this update.

caveats: The patch changes only reader-visible HTTP narrative; the Bundle constraints already carry the conformance requirement.
The current PATCH-related history wording has a separate issue-history conflict and should not be settled through this FHIR-7933-attributed change.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-47211: Align XML signature sigFormat
commits.summary: Aligned the active Digital Signatures page so XML Digital Signature uses Signature.sigFormat application/signature+xml, matching the applied Jira disposition, datatype definition, and examples.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-47211 explicitly approved the XML Digital Signature rule using Signature.sigFormat = application/signature+xml. The active Digital Signatures page instead said application/pkcs7-signature, so this commit restores the approved wording on a reader-visible spec page.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-47211 was applied as Persuasive with Modification for R6 and specifically required the XML Signature Rules sentence to use sigFormat rather than contentType with the value application/signature+xml, while also clarifying that XML DigSig and JSON/JWS are independent of the resource representation and that targetFormat indicates Canonical XML or Canonical JSON. The missed current source surface is source/signatures.html, where the active XML Digital Signature rule used application/pkcs7-signature instead. That page is current specification narrative for digital signatures and the stale value conflicts with both the approved Jira text and the current Signature.sigFormat datatype/examples. Changing that value to application/signature+xml is required to complete the approved application; it is not generated collateral, optional cleanup, or a separate policy change.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/signatures.html is active reader-visible Digital Signatures guidance. The incorrect sigFormat value affects implementer guidance for XML Digital Signatures and contradicts the conformance-facing Signature datatype/examples; this is a current narrative/spec consistency issue, not repository hygiene.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix. If the work group wants XML Digital Signatures to use application/pkcs7-signature instead, handle that through a new final Jira decision with coordinated updates to the signature page, Signature.sigFormat definition, and examples.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution explicitly says the first sentence of the XML Signature Rules should correct contentType to sigFormat and gives the value as application/signature+xml. It also records the approved cross-format clarification and targetFormat Canonical XML/Canonical JSON wording.

FHIR-47211 deferred the separate canonicalization/removing-signature question to this unresolved issue. That deferral limits this commit to the already-approved sigFormat value correction and does not justify changing the MIME value away from application/signature+xml.

caveats: The commit only changes source/signatures.html and does not include generated, derived, or SVG collateral.

A later implementation discussion may explain how application/pkcs7-signature entered the page, but the provided evidence does not show a final Jira or WG disposition superseding FHIR-47211 on this MIME value.

caveats: FHIR-27544 is the direct contradiction issue, but FHIR-25252 and FHIR-40518 supply the most concrete source-wording requirements for the return-parameter and zero-or-more wording.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application for ImagingStudy element ordering. FHIR-47473 accepted concrete moves for the root and series description/endpoint/numberOf* blocks, and the earlier application left several of those accepted ordering moves undone in the authoritative ImagingStudy StructureDefinition.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-47473 was Applied/Persuasive and resolved to update ImagingStudy element order as requested: numberOfSeries and numberOfInstances just before series, description just after identifier, series.description just after series.uid, and endpoint elements just before the corresponding numberOf* elements. The prior application moved only the root numberOfSeries/numberOfInstances pair before series; before this change, ImagingStudy.description still followed note, ImagingStudy.endpoint still appeared above location/reason/note, ImagingStudy.series.description still followed series.modality, and ImagingStudy.series.endpoint still followed series.numberOfInstances. Because source/imagingstudy/structuredefinition-ImagingStudy.xml is the editor-owned StructureDefinition source for the active resource, ElementDefinition ordering affects the generated StructureDefinition and rendered element tables. Moving the existing ElementDefinition blocks, without changing their content, is the necessary remaining source update to complete the accepted ordering-only Jira decision rather than an adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is authoritative conformance source for ImagingStudy. The update changes the order in which these ElementDefinitions appear in generated conformance artifacts and rendered resource tables, while preserving definitions, cardinalities, bindings, mappings, and requirements text.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as the Jira-backed ordering fix for FHIR-47473; no generated or editor-avoided files are included.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue is Applied/Persuasive for FHIR-core ImagingStudy and resolves to update element order as requested. The description requests moving ImagingStudy.numberOfSeries and ImagingStudy.numberOfInstances just before ImagingStudy.series, and pre-resolution comments add exact moves for ImagingStudy.description, ImagingStudy.series.description, and the endpoint elements.

This later Applied endpoint wording change affects the text inside ImagingStudy.endpoint but does not establish a different element order; it supports preserving the current endpoint content while applying the FHIR-47473 move.

This later Applied ImagingStudy.description wording change affects the element text but does not establish a different element order; it supports preserving the current description content while applying the FHIR-47473 move.

caveats: The change is intentionally ordering-only; reviewers should confirm no semantic ElementDefinition content changed if rebasing or replaying it.
Later ImagingStudy wording issues should be preserved, but they do not supersede the FHIR-47473 ordering instruction.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application. FHIR-20176 explicitly required an invariant forbidding bodySite.subSite when bodySite.site is a BodyStructure reference, and the active Claim-family StructureDefinitions still lacked that rule.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-20176 was Published as Persuasive with Modification and required Claim.item.bodySite, ExplanationOfBenefit.item.bodySite, ClaimResponse.addItem.bodySite, and the applied ExplanationOfBenefit.addItem analogue to use a bodySite backbone with site[x] supporting Reference(BodyStructure), subSite as coded detail, and the business rule "if siteReference exists then subSite must not exist." The structural part was applied in the current authoritative StructureDefinition XML as bodySite.site CodeableReference(BodyStructure) plus bodySite.subSite, but the invariant was omitted on the bodySite backbone elements. Because these StructureDefinitions drive the generated conformance resources, rendered constraints, and validator behavior, the omission leaves the current specification permitting instances that the Jira resolution said must be invalid. Adding the site.reference.exists() implies subSite.empty() constraints is the required completion of that Jira application, not optional cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are authoritative StructureDefinition XML for active Claim, ClaimResponse, and ExplanationOfBenefit resources. The added constraints become part of the current conformance definitions and validation rules, preventing BodyStructure references from being combined with subSite contrary to the resolved business rule.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as a Jira-backed source fix. Review it as the missing invariant application for FHIR-20176, while leaving broader BodyStructure guidance and cross-resource bodySite policy to their separate Jira items.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution specifically changed the Claim-family bodySite shape and explicitly required the invariant "if siteReference exists then subSite must not exist." The commit implements that missing rule in the current CodeableReference representation.
This later no-change decision rejected spreading the bodySite.subSite pattern to other resources, supporting the narrow Claim-family scope rather than changing the FHIR-20176 requirement.

This later R6 BodyStructure guidance issue mentions related Claim-family elements but addresses broader OO-owned guidance and cardinality work; it does not supersede the FM invariant required by FHIR-20176.

Those two source surfaces feed current resource maturity metadata in rendered/resource output and build metadata, so they directly conflicted with the normative maturity decision. Setting both values to 6 is required because the FHIR maturity definitions treat FMM 6 as the normative level; this is not adjacent cleanup or generated collateral.

triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix for Condition's R6 maturity metadata. Do not broaden this commit to Condition terminology artifacts or generated diagrams unless a separate terminology or generation decision requires those changes.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive resolution for the FHIR-core Condition artifact says Condition is planned to go normative in R6, satisfying the concrete requirement to update Condition's maturity metadata to the normative FMM level.
Procedure had a parallel Patient Care maturity issue from the same normative-resource discussion, but it applies to a different resource and does not justify the Condition edit.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

commits.summary: Added the missing DICOM EventOutcomeIndicator mapping note to the active AuditEvent outcome comments.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-32445 explicitly required AuditEvent.outcome to document the DICOM EventOutcomeIndicator mapping after moving the outcome value set to issue-severity-based codes. This commit adds that missing note to the authoritative AuditEvent StructureDefinition comments without changing generated or avoided collateral.

The earlier application changed the terminology model but left the active StructureDefinition comments for AuditEvent.outcome and AuditEvent.outcome.code without the required mapping, so the rendered element documentation did not fully apply the Jira resolution. Because StructureDefinition element comments are authoritative current build inputs for rendered element documentation and conformance resource content, omitting the mapping leaves the current spec missing a required explanation for how existing DICOM AuditMessage EventOutcomeIndicator values correspond to the new codes. triage.fhir_spec_impact: The edit affects source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml, an authoritative current AuditEvent StructureDefinition source. Its element comments feed current rendered AuditEvent element documentation and generated conformance content, so the change corrects visible/spec-distributed guidance rather than repository hygiene only.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-32445. Do not reintroduce the old numeric AuditEvent outcome codes; the current issue-severity/success terminology model is preserved and the remaining required change is the mapping note in the StructureDefinition comments.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution specifically required the AuditEvent outcome terminology to use OperationOutcome issue-severity plus success and to update the AuditEvent.outcome comment with the DICOM mapping 0=success, 4=warning, 8=error, and 12=fatal. That exact comment text was the missed source application corrected here.

This related issue about minor/serious outcome definitions was resolved with FHIR-32445, supporting the move away from the old numeric outcome definitions but not independently adding a different required edit for this commit.

This related issue changed AuditEvent.outcome to the current backbone/code model with a required binding, explaining why both AuditEvent.outcome and AuditEvent.outcome.code are relevant current StructureDefinition surfaces for the mapping note.

This later issue added success to issue-severity, preserving the current terminology model in which the mapping note should reference issue-severity-style outcome codes rather than restoring DICOM numeric codes.

Applied/Persuasive issue resolved that the exemplar MedicationRequest administration/category CodeSystem should move to FHIR Core, supporting replacement of old terminology.hl7.org MedicationRequest category systems in current examples.

triage.category_rationale: FHIR-31481's resolution was Persuasive/Applied and explicitly said to change the SubstanceDefinition.domain definition from "If the substance applies to only human or veterinary use" to "The applicable usage of the substance, as an example human or veterinary." The StructureDefinition element wording was already updated, but the active SubstanceDefinition-domain SearchParameter description still used the exact rejected human/veterinary-only phrase. Because the search parameter bundle is the source for the published SearchParameter conformance resource, the stale description remains implementer-visible current specification content. Its description feeds the current SearchParameter definition for SubstanceDefinition.domain, so the stale wording affects published conformance/implementer-facing search parameter text rather than only repository hygiene.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as the Jira-backed completion of FHIR-31481 for the active SearchParameter source.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue requested and the WG accepted replacing the old SubstanceDefinition.domain wording with broader applicable-usage wording. The edited SearchParameter description was a remaining active conformance-source copy of the old wording for the same domain concept.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-17722: Align Address.type location guidance
commits.summary: Corrected the remaining contradictory Address.type comment so it no longer quotes the obsolete postal-not-physical wording.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-17722 replaced the obsolete Address note that contrasted postal addresses with physical locations, but the Address.type comment still quoted that obsolete wording. This one-line datatype source edit aligns the remaining Address.type guidance with the approved administrative-purpose/absolute-coordinate wording while preserving physical-address guidance.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-17722 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and specifically resolved the Address contradiction by changing the note from "postal addresses, not physical locations" to wording that Address describes postal addresses for administrative purposes, not absolute geographical coordinates, and that postal addresses are often proxies for physical locations. The historical application updated the root Address comment but left the Address.type comment saying the definition stated the obsolete postal-not-physical wording, so the current datatype source still repeated the contradiction the Jira resolved. source/datatypes/address.xml is the authoritative datatype spreadsheet source for rendered Address datatype content and generated element comments, so the stale Address.type comment affects current reader-facing/conformance guidance rather than only repository cleanliness. Rewording this specific comment is required to complete the Jira application because it removes the remaining obsolete quote without changing unrelated Address semantics or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is authoritative datatype source, and the Address.type comment is part of the current Address datatype documentation and generated element guidance. The edit affects current rendered/conformance-facing wording by removing an obsolete statement that directly conflicted with the approved Address note; it is not a generated-file or layout-only cleanup.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-17722. No subset omission is needed because the commit touches only the editor-owned datatype source surface.

jira_evidence.explanation: The approved resolution replaced the old Address note saying addresses were postal, not physical locations, with administrative-purpose/absolute-coordinate wording plus the statement that postal addresses may proxy physical locations. The remaining Address.type comment quoted the old wording, so this edit is needed to finish applying that resolution.

This earlier published clarification introduced the nearby physical-address guidance. It supports preserving the Address.type discussion of visitable/delivery use while aligning it with the later FHIR-17722 wording.
This adjacent Location.address issue concerned Location-specific address comments and does not supersede the Address datatype wording resolved by FHIR-17722.
This later official-address issue concerns Address.use or extension requirements, not the postal-versus-physical wording addressed here.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

The authoritative Group StructureDefinition and notes had already been updated, but source/fhir.ini's active [r5-r6-changes] section still listed Group.characteristic.timing=+, so the R5-to-R6 metadata omitted the final current element name and retained a removed draft name. commits.author: Josh Mandel

commits.summary: ResearchSubject.subject now includes NutritionProduct as an approved non-patient subject target, completing the same target-family decision that had previously added BiologicallyDerivedProduct but omitted NutritionProduct.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-31351 explicitly accepted NutritionProduct as a ResearchSubject.subject target, but the historical R5 application added the rest of the target family and left NutritionProduct out. The single changed file is the authoritative ResearchSubject StructureDefinition, so this is an appropriate source fix.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-31351 was resolved Persuasive with Modification with the concrete requirement to add BiologicallyDerivedProduct and NutritionProduct to the ResearchSubject individual/subject reference target set, while deferring Procedure. The current source had ResearchSubject.subject renamed and widened to Patient, Group, Specimen, Device, Medication, Substance, SubstanceDefinition, and BiologicallyDerivedProduct, but still omitted NutritionProduct after NutritionProduct became an active core resource. Because targetProfile entries in the StructureDefinition drive the generated conformance resource, rendered element type list, and validation expectations for ResearchSubject.subject, the omission leaves the current specification narrower than the approved Jira disposition. Adding the NutritionProduct targetProfile is the necessary editor-owned source change to complete that Jira application; no generated or layout-only files are included.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed XML is authoritative conformance source for ResearchSubject. Adding NutritionProduct changes the allowed Reference target profiles exposed in current conformance output and rendered element details for ResearchSubject.subject, rather than only cleaning repository text or generated collateral.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-31351. Regenerate diagrams or other derived artifacts only through the normal build process if needed; do not hand-edit SVG collateral for this change.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue requested that ResearchSubject.individual, now ResearchSubject.subject, not be limited to Patient for studies involving non-human or non-animal items. Its resolution and comments specifically say to add BiologicallyDerivedProduct and NutritionProduct and defer Procedure, which directly requires NutritionProduct in the ResearchSubject.subject target list once the resource exists.

This companion ResearchSubject issue accepted widening the same element to Patient, Group, Specimen, Device, Medication, and Substance. It explains the related target-family change that was applied together with FHIR-31351 but does not itself require NutritionProduct.

This issue renamed ResearchSubject.individual to ResearchSubject.subject in the same historical application, confirming that the FHIR-31351 target-profile requirement now belongs on ResearchSubject.subject.
This later issue added SubstanceDefinition to the same target set after the Substance instance/definition split. It is useful current context but is not the justification for adding NutritionProduct.

caveats: The historical omission appears tied to the contemporaneous Jira comment that there was no NutritionProduct resource at the time; that no longer applies in the current source tree.
The commit only changes source/researchsubject/structuredefinition-ResearchSubject.xml and does not include generated-looking SVG or model collateral.

The strongest Jira evidence is for the model changes, element descriptions, and ClinicalUseDefinition scope narrative. The module overview and root summary alignment are reasonable current-spec fixes but weaker as exact FHIR-31394 obligations.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

Because `source/secpriv-module.html` is a current narrative page, the stale token is reader-visible Security guidance rather than inert repository residue. Replacing `_revinc` with `_revinclude` is the narrow change required to complete the intended Jira application; it is not generated collateral, optional broad consistency cleanup, or a later policy change.

triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed narrative correction for FHIR-13822.

jira_evidence.explanation: The published persuasive-with-modification resolution required adding the Query Parameters Considerations subsection and its unauthorized-query-parameter example. commits.author: Josh Mandel

triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an editor-owned StructureDefinition source for CapabilityStatement. triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as the Jira-backed fix for the CapabilityStatement conformance text. No subset should be dropped; the duplicate FHIR-13828 needs no separate change.

jira_evidence.explanation: Resolved Persuasive with Modification to replace blanket CORS guidance with conditional wording for browser-based JavaScript clients and references to security guidance; this directly conflicts with the old CapabilityStatement comment saying all servers should support CORS and showing permissive wildcard headers.

commits.subject: FHIR-36401: Align single vital-sign invariant keys

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-36401 required the single-value vital-sign profiles to enforce that either Observation.value[x] or Observation.dataAbsentReason is present. The current profile source contains that invariant, but its key did not match the condition references on value[x] and dataAbsentReason, leaving the formal constraint wiring inconsistent.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-36401 was applied with a requirement that simple vital-sign observations must not rely only on Observation.component for the result and must have Observation.value[x] or Observation.dataAbsentReason; the later application notes and commits applied that rule across the same eight single-value vital-sign profiles changed here. The missed application is concrete: each affected StructureDefinition had an invariant keyed as vs-4 while the relevant Observation.valueQuantity and Observation.dataAbsentReason elements referenced condition vsp-4, so the approved rule was present but not formally resolvable from the elements that should carry it. These profile XML files are authoritative current-build conformance inputs for Observation, so the mismatch affects generated StructureDefinitions and validation/QA behavior rather than only source-tree neatness. Renaming the invariant key to vsp-4 is required to complete the Jira application because it aligns the existing approved expression with the existing condition references without introducing a new rule or broader component-role policy.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are active Observation profile StructureDefinition sources for BMI, body height, body temperature, body weight, head circumference, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate. The edit affects current conformance output by making each element condition reference resolve to the intended value-or-dataAbsentReason invariant; it is not a generated-only, diagram, or repository-hygiene change.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source fix as a Jira-backed correction to the FHIR-36401 application. No subset should be dropped; all touched files are editor-owned StructureDefinition sources for the same invariant wiring issue.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution required simple vital-sign profiles to state and enforce that Observation.value[x] or Observation.dataAbsentReason is valued instead of allowing the result only in Observation.component. The applied Jira comments and historical commits added that rule to the same eight single-value vital-sign profiles, but the remaining source had the invariant key and condition references out of sync.
This related vital-sign profile cleanup adjusted pattern and slicing behavior in the same profile family, but it does not provide the rule being fixed here.

This later vital-sign cleanup changed Observation.component MustSupport placement and related binding/profile organization, but the invariant requirement and key mismatch are attributable to FHIR-36401.
This later issue clarified vital-sign summary wording to match constraints; it supports the surrounding vital-signs cleanup history but is not the source of this formal invariant-key repair.
This later issue clarified Vital Signs Panel hasMember/value wording and is adjacent context only; it does not justify the single-value profile invariant-key change.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider adding a publisher or QA check that flags ElementDefinition.condition values that do not resolve to a constraint key in the same StructureDefinition.
caveats: The broader future consideration in FHIR-36401 about result, qualifier, and supplemental component roles remains separate; this commit only repairs the already-applied value-or-dataAbsentReason invariant wiring.
No hard-avoid generated files or SVGs are touched.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-7888: Generalize Encounter participant definition
commits.summary: Generalized the active Encounter.participant definition from people-only wording to participant-neutral wording and synchronized the parallel mapping exception and SVG tooltip.

triage.reviewer_summary: Real Encounter definition fix needing cleaner attribution: the current parent definition says Encounter participants are people responsible for the service, but the current actor targets include non-person participants such as Device and HealthcareService. The shown Jira explains the original move away from practitioner-only wording, but it did not itself require this later participant-neutral wording.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-7888 resolved the original DSTU1 problem by changing Encounter.participant from a main-practitioner definition to "The list of people responsible for providing the service," so that decision was historically applied rather than missed. Later published PA decisions broadened Encounter.participant.actor beyond people, making the inherited parent definition stale in current conformance output, but those decisions primarily specified actor target/type changes and actor wording rather than expressly requiring this parent-definition text and mapping-exception update.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition hunk affects current Encounter conformance and rendered element definition text, so leaving "people responsible" is misleading for allowed non-person actor targets. The mapping exception hunk keeps the Event/Encounter divergence metadata aligned with the same definition, but it is supporting collateral rather than the primary conformance source.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Consider applying the StructureDefinition wording fix under the later Encounter participant actor decisions, or under a small cleanup/rollup issue if reviewers want explicit attribution for the parent definition and mapping exception. Do not treat FHIR-7888 alone as a clean missed application because its accepted wording was the people-responsible text now being replaced.

jira_evidence.explanation: This issue required replacing "The main practitioner responsible for providing the service" with "The list of people responsible for providing the service." That explains why practitioner-only wording was wrong, but it does not require replacing the accepted people wording with participant-neutral text.
This later Encounter decision added Device as an Encounter.participant actor target and renamed individual to actor, making the participant model broader than people.

This later PA decision updated Encounter.participant.actor to include Patient, Group, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, RelatedPerson, Device, and HealthcareService. It is the strongest attribution for why the parent participant definition should not be limited to people, although it did not spell out this exact parent-definition edit.

This issue aligned Encounter.participant.actor wording to "The individual, device, or service participating in the encounter," confirming the current participant actor semantics include non-person participants but focusing on actor rather than the parent participant definition.

caveats: The commit does not include a hard-avoid SVG/generated file; both changed files are source-side XML.
The mapping exception update should be reviewed as supporting alignment with the StructureDefinition hunk, not as an independent Jira-required conformance change.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-38688: Complete locale warnings for search text
commits.summary: Completed the published locale warning clarification on the FHIR search page.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-38688 explicitly approved locale/implementation-dependent guidance for case-insensitive search text handling and sorting on the search page. This commit completes that guidance in the remaining relevant search-page sections and removes it from exact matching, where it was incorrectly applied.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-38688 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and resolved to add the proposed guidance to the string search type and relevant modifiers; the request specifically called out case-insensitive text searching and sorting as locale-dependent because character case definitions and conversions are outside FHIR. The current source/search.html application was incomplete: the text modifier, text-advanced modifier, and string sorting prose still described case-insensitive behavior without that warning, while exact matching retained the warning even though exact matching includes casing. source/search.html is the source for the rendered search page, so these omissions and the misplaced warning affect current reader-visible normative guidance about search and sort behavior. The edit is needed to finish the approved clarification on the actual affected surfaces, not merely to do consistency cleanup: it adds the warning where the approved case-insensitive behavior is described and removes it from a section where the approved rationale does not apply.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative HTML source for the rendered FHIR search page. The update changes reader-visible guidance for reference/token text matching, text-advanced matching, exact string matching, and string sorting; it does not touch generated collateral or repository-only metadata.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed completion of FHIR-38688 for source/search.html.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was Published/Persuasive and resolved to add the proposed guidance to the string search type and relevant modifiers. The issue description names case-insensitive text searching and sorting on the search page and asks for explicit guidance that character case definitions and conversions are outside FHIR and therefore implementation dependent across locales.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-36341: Use OBX-6 in Quantity V2 mappings
commits.summary: Corrected the remaining active OBX-6 separator text tied to the Observation V2 mapping issue.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: keep the Quantity datatype mapping edit. FHIR-36341 required OBX field references in the Observation V2 mapping material, including OBX.6, to use hyphen field notation, and the active Quantity mapping still exposed the same OBX.6 separator error in the OBX quantity unit/code mapping.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-36341 was Published/Persuasive and specifically requested the V2 field-versus-component separator correction for Observation mappings, naming OBX.6 as a field reference that should use a hyphen. The prior application fixed the direct Observation StructureDefinition mappings, but source/datatypes/quantity.xml still had Quantity.unit, Quantity.system, and Quantity.code V2 cells saying `(see OBX.6 etc.) / CQ.2`. Those cells are authoritative datatype mapping source for Quantity, so the missed text affects current rendered/datatype mapping and conformance-source content rather than only repository cleanliness. The proposed edit is necessary and narrow because it changes only the named field reference from OBX.6 to OBX-6 while preserving CQ.2 as a component reference.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/datatypes/quantity.xml is an editor-owned datatype spreadsheet source, and its V2 mapping cells feed the current Quantity mapping/StructureDefinition content. Leaving OBX.6 there would keep a current spec mapping with the exact field separator error the approved Jira correction was meant to remove; no generated, layout-only, or ignored files are involved.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a bounded Jira-backed source fix. Review it as the remaining active Quantity datatype mapping application of the approved OBX-6 separator correction, without expanding the change to unrelated resources.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested hyphen notation for V2 field references in the Observation mapping material, explicitly listing OBX.6 among the entries to correct. The changed Quantity V2 mapping cells still used OBX.6 for the OBX quantity unit/code reference, so this is the remaining active source application of that approved separator rule.

This separate ServiceRequest issue used the same reporter, work group vote, and V2 separator rule, supporting the general hyphen-for-fields and dot-for-components convention but not serving as the direct attribution for this Quantity OBX-6 edit.

caveats: FHIR-36341 was raised against Observation, and the direct Observation rows were already fixed in the original application; this commit is limited to the active Quantity datatype rows that still referenced the same OBX-6 field using dot notation.
CQ.2 remains unchanged because it is a datatype component reference, not a v2 segment-field reference.
