commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-39141 + FHIR-47297: Clarify Transport business status boundary
commits.summary: Updated the active Transport boundaries narrative so patient movement remains separated from encounter business status while current Transport.reason retains its later-approved why-transport-is-needed meaning.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application, with mixed attribution: the Transport boundary paragraph still told readers to use Transport.reason for current encounter business status even after later approved changes made Transport.reason the why-transport-is-needed element and added Encounter.businessStatus for current encounter business states.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-39141 required Transport.reasonCode and Transport.reasonReference to be replaced by repeatable Transport.reason with the meaning 'Why transport is needed', and FHIR-40310 later confirmed that Transport.reason should keep that role rather than be renamed. FHIR-47297 required current encounter business statuses to be represented on Encounter.businessStatus, while FHIR-36248 required the Transport Boundaries and Relationships narrative to distinguish physical movement from patient class or level-of-care business-state changes. The current Transport boundary text missed that combined application because it still said current patient business status should be captured with the reason element. That paragraph is rendered reader-facing Transport narrative and directly contradicted the current Transport.reason and Encounter.businessStatus semantics. The proposed edit is the targeted authoritative-source change needed to complete the application: it preserves the required movement/business-status boundary, points current encounter business status to Encounter.businessStatus, and limits Transport.reason to why the transport is needed.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The only changed file is source/transport/transport-introduction.xml, the Transport Boundaries and Relationships narrative. This affects rendered specification guidance for Transport readers; without the fix, the page directs implementers to put encounter business status in Transport.reason even though current conformance definitions assign Transport.reason to transport rationale and Encounter.businessStatus to current encounter business status.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the narrative fix, but treat the attribution as shared: FHIR-36248 explains why the boundary text exists, while FHIR-39141/FHIR-40310 and FHIR-47297 explain why the current wording must change. Any further direct historical EncounterHistory linkage should be handled as a separate OO/PA decision.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution replaced Transport.reasonCode and Transport.reasonReference with repeatable Transport.reason, explicitly defined as why transport is needed. That makes the existing boundary sentence directing current business status to the reason element stale and contradictory.

The resolution added Encounter.businessStatus for current encounter business statuses and says historical business statuses belong in EncounterHistory. This provides the current authoritative target for the patient class or level-of-care status guidance.

The resolution required the Transport Boundaries and Relationships section to explain the separation between physical movement and patient business-state changes. Its original reason-based application was later superseded, but the boundary guidance remains necessary.

The resolution confirmed that Transport.reason did not need renaming after reasonCode was removed and kept the element focused on transport rationale, reinforcing that it should not be used as the encounter business-status field.

caveats: The shown issue key is relevant but not complete attribution: the stale paragraph originates from the FHIR-36248 boundary work, while later Transport and Encounter decisions make the corrected wording necessary.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-38034: Complete derived OperationDefinition guidance
commits.summary: Completed the derived OperationDefinition guidance application by removing stale moved guidance from OperationDefinition.base and clarifying the notes sentence that introduces base derivation.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application for derived OperationDefinition guidance. FHIR-38034 specifically required moving the OperationDefinition.base derivation guidance into notes and explaining that a derived OperationDefinition declares its base; the earlier application left that source surface partly stale.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-38034 was resolved as Persuasive for R5 with concrete instructions to move the comment on OperationDefinition.base into a separate "Deriving operations" notes section, reword the constrained-operation guidance there, state that a derived operation defines a base and must respect existing parameter constraints, and point to an example. The existing source had added the notes section and example pointer but still left the old "A constrained profile can..." guidance in the OperationDefinition.base element comment, while the note sentence introducing base declaration was malformed. OperationDefinition's StructureDefinition XML is the authoritative conformance source for the element comment, and operationdefinition-notes.xml is reader-visible resource narrative, so the stale split affects current rendered/conformance guidance rather than only repository cleanliness. This edit is necessary to finish the resolved Jira application because it removes the guidance from the element comment as requested, keeps the later version-specific canonical-reference advice, and makes the notes text directly state that a derived OperationDefinition declares a base.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are editor-owned OperationDefinition source: the StructureDefinition element comment feeds generated definitions/conformance presentation for OperationDefinition.base, and the notes file feeds rendered OperationDefinition guidance. The update removes obsolete duplicated derivation behavior text from the element comment and fixes the reader-visible sentence that introduces derived OperationDefinition base declaration.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as the focused completion of the FHIR-38034 application. No subset should be dropped; the later FHIR-48481 canonical-reference wording is preserved rather than overwritten.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution explicitly required moving the OperationDefinition.base comment guidance into a separate "Deriving operations" notes section and stating that a derived operation defines a base, may keep or change code, and must respect existing parameter constraints. That directly requires removing the moved guidance from the base element comment and ensuring the notes introduce base declaration clearly.

This later applied R6 issue required version-specific canonical-reference guidance on OperationDefinition.base. It supports preserving that sentence while removing only the older constrained-profile guidance that FHIR-38034 said to move into notes.
The referenced later parameter/profile alignment guidance is separate context in the same notes area and does not replace the FHIR-38034 requirement. It does not independently justify this edit.

caveats: This judgment depends on treating operationdefinition-notes.xml and structuredefinition-OperationDefinition.xml as authoritative current-build source, not generated collateral.
FHIR-48481 narrows the safe edit by requiring the version-specific canonical-reference advice to remain in OperationDefinition.base.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

Procedure is an active core resource and its notes file is Procedure narrative content, so the stale term affects current rendered guidance rather than only repository cleanliness. Replacing "indication" with "reason" is the narrow edit required to complete the Jira rename in this narrative surface; it is not generated collateral or optional consistency cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/procedure/procedure-notes.xml is active Procedure narrative source. Before this edit, the rendered Procedure guidance referred to an element name that no longer exists, while the conformance source exposes Procedure.reason; the change aligns reader-visible narrative with current conformance content.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as a Jira-backed fix to the Procedure narrative note. No generated files or extension-pack changes are part of this source correction.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution explicitly said to rename Procedure.indication to reason[x] and allow CodeableConcept or Condition reference. That directly requires active Procedure source and narrative guidance not to continue naming an "indication" property.
FHIR-7127 referenced this related CarePlan/request work for part of the old relatedItem scope, but it is not needed to justify the note wording change from indication to reason.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-5276 required Observation.name to become Observation.code, and the profiling narrative still contained reader-visible discriminator examples using the old Observation.name path. This commit updates only the editor-owned profiling page text needed to align those examples with the current Observation StructureDefinition.
triage.category_rationale: Resolution gate: FHIR-5276 was Published/Persuasive and specifically accepted the change from existing wording Observation.name to proposed wording Observation.code because the element carries a coded observation identifier. Missed-application gate: source/profiling.html still used Observation.name.extension, Observation.name, item.resolve().name, and a "name element" explanation for examples that point to an Observation target even though the active Observation definition has Observation.code. Current spec-impact gate: source/profiling.html is the rendered profiling guidance page, so these stale examples would teach profile authors invalid current discriminator paths against Observation. Necessity gate: replacing those exact paths and explanatory terms with code is the direct completion of the accepted rename in this reader-visible guidance, not generated collateral or optional cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The change affects rendered profiling guidance and examples for slicing/discriminator use. It does not change generated conformance resources, but it removes invalid reader-facing element paths that conflict with the current Observation.code element.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source/profiling.html update as the Jira-backed correction; no generated or layout-only files need to be reviewed with it.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive OO ballot resolution explicitly accepted changing Observation.name to Observation.code; the unchanged profiling examples still referenced the old element name for Observation paths.

This Published technical correction identified the same profiling page as needing a name-to-code wording fix after the Observation rename, but its applied change covered a different sentence and mainly corroborates that this page was part of the missed-reference family.

caveats: The commit touches only source/profiling.html, an editor-owned narrative page; there are no SVG, generated, or derived-file hunks to omit.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-7175: Clarify NutritionOrder food preference modifier
commits.summary: Clarified the active NutritionOrder.foodPreferenceModifier definition so it reflects patient preferences rather than deriving the element from allergies or intolerances.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-7175 kept NutritionOrder.foodPreferenceModifier as a distinct way to record food preferences rather than allergy or intolerance semantics. The current StructureDefinition definition still said the element could be derived from allergies or intolerances, so this narrow source edit completes the published clarification.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-7175 resolved the ballot comment on NutritionOrder.foodPreferenceModifier by deciding that preferences and intolerances are clinically different and that the resource needs a separate way to record food preferences. The missed application is the active NutritionOrder.foodPreferenceModifier definition, which still stated that these modifiers can be derived from patient allergies, intolerances, or preferences even though the neighboring comment and binding are preference-specific. Because this definition is in the authoritative NutritionOrder StructureDefinition, the stale wording affects generated conformance content and rendered element-definition text. Removing allergy/intolerance derivation from this definition is necessary to complete the FHIR-7175 distinction, while leaving AllergyIntolerance and excludeFoodModifier guidance to FHIR-7176 and later FHIR-46700.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/nutritionorder/structuredefinition-NutritionOrder.xml is an authoritative StructureDefinition input for NutritionOrder. The changed definition is rendered as element documentation and carried in generated conformance resources, so stale allergy/intolerance wording would misstate the current semantics of foodPreferenceModifier rather than being repository-only cleanup.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix for NutritionOrder.foodPreferenceModifier. Do not expand it into excludeFoodModifier or AllergyIntolerance changes; those related surfaces are covered by FHIR-7176 and FHIR-46700.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue specifically challenged NutritionOrder.foodPreferenceModifier because of confusion between intolerance and preference; the published resolution kept the field because there is a clinical difference and a need to record preferences separately. That directly requires the element definition not to present allergy or intolerance derivation as part of foodPreferenceModifier semantics.

The companion issue addressed excludeFoodModifier and required text saying allergy or intolerance information should not need to be repeated there. It supports the same distinction but does not replace the direct FHIR-7175 basis for the foodPreferenceModifier definition.

This later NutritionOrder clarification refined excludeFoodModifier as complementing but not duplicating AllergyIntolerance. It reinforces the separation of allergy/intolerance handling from preference and exclusion guidance, but the needed foodPreferenceModifier edit is already justified by FHIR-7175.

caveats: The commit changes only the authoritative NutritionOrder StructureDefinition and does not include generated, derived, or layout-only files.
FHIR-7176 and FHIR-46700 should remain the attribution for excludeFoodModifier guidance; this commit should stay limited to foodPreferenceModifier.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-27789: Require absolute canonical URL regex
commits.summary: Completed the published FHIR-27789 decision by tightening canonical resource URL invariants so canonical URLs must include an absolute URI scheme colon.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-27789 explicitly required CanonicalResource.url to be an absolute URI and to have a computable regex requiring a colon. The existing cnl-1 invariant still allowed relative canonical URLs, so tightening the invariant in the authoritative StructureDefinition sources completes the published decision.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-27789 resolved that CanonicalResource.url SHALL be an absolute URI and that the regex include a ':' requirement in addition to excluding spaces. The current source had only partially applied that decision: the wording said absolute URI, but CanonicalResource.url and the active URL elements carrying cnl-1 still used a regex such as ^[^|# ]+$, which rejects pipes, hashes, and spaces but accepts relative strings without a URI scheme. These StructureDefinition XML files are authoritative conformance inputs, so the stale invariant affects rendered constraint text and validation/QA behavior for canonical-resource URL elements. Updating the human text and FHIRPath regex on CanonicalResource.url and its copied/inherited active URL constraints is necessary to make the computable rule match the Jira decision, not merely adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are editor-owned StructureDefinition XML sources. Their short descriptions and cnl-1 constraints feed current rendered element pages, generated conformance resources, and validation warning behavior for canonical resource URLs; before this change, the computable constraint contradicted the absolute-URI requirement by permitting relative values.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as the Jira-backed fix, subject to normal editorial review of the exact regex and the list of active URL elements carrying the canonical URL constraint.

jira_evidence.explanation: The published persuasive resolution specifically says CanonicalResource.url SHALL be an absolute URI and that the regex should require ':' in addition to the no-spaces URI baseline. That directly requires a computable colon/scheme check on the canonical URL invariant.

This later issue introduced the cnl-1 invariant across CanonicalResource.url and inherited URL elements to exclude '|' and '#'. It explains why the current invariant exists, but it did not satisfy FHIR-27789's separate colon requirement.

caveats: No hard-avoid generated files or layout-only SVGs are included; the commit changes only StructureDefinition XML conformance sources.
The regex preserves urn:oid: and urn:uuid: forms because it requires a URI scheme followed by ':' rather than requiring http(s).

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-27113: Correct REST trailing slash example
commits.summary: Corrected the RESTful API trailing-slash paragraph so the non-trailing resource-type example is the valid form [base]/[type].

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-27113 required the RESTful HTTP page to state that resource-type endpoints with and without a trailing slash are equivalent when either form is supported. The original application left the non-trailing example malformed as [base]/type], and this commit corrects that rendered normative example.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-27113 was resolved Persuasive with Modification with concrete REST wording: servers SHALL support both forms, with and without a trailing slash, if they support either, should not redirect merely to canonicalize the query URL, and may choose their preferred convention for Bundle.link[self]. The original application added that paragraph to source/http.html but left the non-trailing URL example as [base]/type], which is malformed and fails to show the required equivalent [base]/[type] form. Because source/http.html is the active RESTful API page, the malformed example appears in current reader-visible normative HTTP guidance. Correcting it to [base]/[type], with punctuation cleanup in the same sentence, is required to complete the approved Jira application rather than optional adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The change affects source/http.html, the rendered RESTful API specification page. It corrects a malformed example inside a SHALL paragraph; it does not change conformance resources or generated collateral, but it directly improves current rendered normative guidance.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix to the RESTful HTTP page. Review it as a narrow correction to the originally approved trailing-slash rule, not as a reopening of the server redirect or canonicalization policy.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Jira was Published/Persuasive with Modification and specifically required RESTful HTTP language treating resource-type URLs with and without a trailing slash as equivalent when either form is supported. The initial application added that paragraph but malformed the non-trailing example, so this correction is directly required by the resolved wording.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-31491: Align named-query parameter scope notes
commits.summary: Aligned the OperationDefinition named-query notes with the FHIR-31491 Search-page rule for inherited search-parameter scope and support.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a real fix needing attribution or work-group confirmation: it removes a reader-visible inconsistency between the Search and OperationDefinition named-query guidance. It should not be treated as a clean missed application of FHIR-31491 because the OperationDefinition wording being changed appears to come from a later named-query Jira with its own resolution text.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-31491 clearly established the Search-page rule that inherited named-query search parameters are only potentially available, that resource-specific parameters depend on the query operation's resource scope, and that server support is constrained by documentation and CapabilityStatement expectations. The current OperationDefinition notes paragraph is an active narrative surface and conflicts with that rule by using older automatic-scope wording, tying resource-specific parameters to resources returned by the operation, and saying supported parameters must be listed in OperationDefinition. However, the evidence does not make this a clean Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-31491's concrete resolution targeted the Search section, while the OperationDefinition paragraph aligns closely with the later FHIR-39318 resolution language. Correcting the cross-page inconsistency is substantively appropriate, but it changes or reconciles a later work-group-resolved paragraph and should have an explicit attribution or confirmation path.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the OperationDefinition resource notes narrative, so the text is reader-visible on the current OperationDefinition page. The change affects how implementers understand named-query inherited search-parameter scope and support; it does not change conformance resource structure, validation rules, examples, or generated-only collateral.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Consider the edit as a real OperationDefinition/Search consistency fix, but route it through FHIR-I confirmation or a follow-up issue that explicitly reconciles FHIR-31491 and FHIR-39318 rather than applying it solely as a missed FHIR-31491 application.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution directly defines the desired named-query semantics for standard, resource-scoped, and inherited search parameters, server support, CapabilityStatement assumptions, and optional documentation of supported parameters. It strongly supports the substance of the proposed wording, but its concrete source instruction was to replace text in the Search section, not to revise the later OperationDefinition notes paragraph.

This later named-query issue specifically requested OperationDefinition-page narrative and its resolution text closely matches the paragraph being changed, including common/resource-returned parameters and explicit OperationDefinition listing. That makes it the more relevant attribution for the current OperationDefinition surface, but it does not by itself justify replacing that wording with the FHIR-31491/Search-page formulation.

The named-query examples discussion supports treating resource-scoped parameters such as Patient.birthdate as usable in Patient-scoped named queries when supported, but it does not require this specific OperationDefinition notes edit.

caveats: There are no generated, derived, SVG, or editor-avoided files in this commit; the concern is attribution and decision authority, not file scope.

The Search page already contains the FHIR-31491 wording, while the OperationDefinition notes paragraph currently reflects later FHIR-39318-style wording, so reviewers should decide whether the later paragraph was an intentional narrowing or an inconsistency to correct.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-27832: Clarify package example folder path
commits.summary: Clarified the active FHIR NPM package specification so JSON example resources are documented at /package/example and all additional folders and files are below /package.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-27832 required the package specification to clarify where JSON examples live and that extra package content sits under the package folder. The active NPM Packages page still described an `examples` folder while the same page and current package practice use `/package/example`.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-27832 was resolved as a persuasive technical correction to clarify that package examples, when present, are JSON and that additional package folders are subfolders of the package folder rather than siblings. The prior application added JSON and under-package wording, but left the main package-structure bullet naming an `examples` folder and left the additional-folder sentence grammatically ambiguous about whether files were also below `package`; this conflicted with the same page's IG package description using `/package/example`. `source/packages.html` is the active NPM Packages source page, so the stale wording affects rendered package-layout guidance read by implementers. The proposed edit is required to finish the original correction because it makes the primary structure list name the actual `/package/example` path and makes both additional folders and files clearly subordinate to the package folder, rather than adding unrelated cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The only changed file is `source/packages.html`, which is included as the current NPM Packages page. The change affects reader-visible package-structure documentation, not generated artifacts or repository-only metadata.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix for the active package-spec page. Do not expand it to XML package documentation without a separate work-group decision.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was resolved persuasive as a FHIR-core technical correction to clarify that package examples are JSON and that every additional folder is below the package folder. That directly supports correcting the active package-structure text so examples are documented at the current `/package/example` location and extra content is described under `package`.

caveats: FHIR-I minutes noted XML package documentation as separate future work; this commit appropriately stays limited to the JSON package documentation surface.
The singular `/package/example` path is also supported by the same page's IG package-type text and current package artifacts.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-26944: Complete position discriminator guidance
commits.summary: Completed the R5 position discriminator guidance by adding the approved $this path and single-discriminator restriction to the ElementDefinition code-list source and profiling narrative.
commits.stat:
source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml | 2 +-
 source/profiling.html                  | 2 ++
 2 files changed, 3 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-26944 approved the R5 position discriminator together with concrete usage constraints, but the existing source only carried over the code and cardinality rule. This commit completes the authoritative ElementDefinition code-list text and profiling narrative with the approved `$this` path and single-discriminator restriction.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-26944 was Published/Persuasive and its resolution required introducing ElementDefinition.slicing.discriminator.type = `position` and explaining the constraints documented in the Jira comment: the discriminator path is `$this`, all but the last slice need fixed cardinality, and `position` is not to be combined with other discriminator entries. The existing ElementDefinition spreadsheet code-list definition and profiling.html guidance already contained `position` and the fixed-cardinality rule, but omitted the approved `$this` path and prohibition on multiple discriminator entries. Those surfaces feed current conformance/narrative guidance for profiling, so the omission leaves the rendered/current specification incomplete about how a valid position discriminator is represented. The proposed edits add exactly the missing approved constraints in the editor-owned authoritative sources, rather than optional cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The ElementDefinition spreadsheet source supplies the discriminator type code definition used in the generated conformance/rendered datatype material, and profiling.html is built reader-facing profiling guidance. Leaving out the path and single-discriminator rule makes the current specification understate the approved semantics of `position` slicing and can mislead profile authors and implementers about valid discriminator declarations.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-26944. Any additional enforcement, such as a formal invariant for the single-discriminator rule, should be handled separately if the work group wants tooling-level validation.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive resolution says to introduce discriminator type `position` and explain its use and constraints as documented in the Jira comment; that comment specifically identifies `$this` as the path and records the agreement to prohibit use of `position` in an array with other discriminators.

The earlier rank/position slicing issue explains the same problem space but resolved with ordered slicing and no new discriminator. It does not itself require this edit; FHIR-26944 is the later direct decision for the explicit `position` discriminator.

caveats: This commit updates only editor-owned source files and does not include hard-avoid generated, derived, or SVG collateral.
The commit documents the approved rule but does not add a validator invariant; that narrower scope matches the missed source application.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-19608: Fix translation extension JSON example
commits.summary: Fixed a current build-scoped translation-extension JSON example that still had malformed url properties.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application, but with mixed attribution: the source hunk is directly required by the datatype JSON examples work, while the cited translation-extension issue is supporting context for the specific syntax shape. The commit fixes a reader-visible malformed JSON example in the ElementDefinition examples page.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-19608 resolved that datatype examples should be available in JSON as well as XML, with tabs for the alternate representations; for the ElementDefinition examples page, that concretely requires the JSON tab content to be syntactically usable JSON for the corresponding example. The current source surface missed that requirement because source/elementdefinition-examples.html still contained a FHIR-19608-added Coding.display translation-extension JSON fragment with malformed url properties, leaving `"url" : "lang"" : {` and `"url" : "content"" : {` in a `<pre class="json">` block. That block is editor-owned narrative source under the current DataTypes > ElementDefinition page tree, so the defect is rendered as an invalid JSON example rather than being stripped or confined to generated collateral. Replacing the malformed url fragments with normal `url` properties followed by valueCode/valueString is the minimal necessary edit to complete the JSON-example application while preserving the intended translation extension structure.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an included handwritten HTML examples page, not a generated artifact or checked example that the publisher can silently normalize. The stale text appears in a JSON display block for a current ElementDefinition example, so it affects reader-visible specification content by showing invalid JSON for a translation extension on Coding.display.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source fix, but cite FHIR-19608 as the direct missed application for the ElementDefinition examples page and FHIR-26841 only as supporting context for the translation-extension JSON syntax.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution required datatype examples to be available in JSON as well as XML. The malformed fragment was introduced by the JSON-example application in source/elementdefinition-examples.html, so a syntactically invalid JSON block is an incomplete application of that decision on the exact edited page.

This issue resolved that missing or misplaced punctuation in the Translation extension JSON display should be fixed, and it supports the corrected nested lang/content structure. Its described surface was the translation extension page, however, so it does not by itself prove that the ElementDefinition examples page was a missed application.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider validating included `<pre class="json">` example blocks, or otherwise flagging malformed JSON fragments in rendered narrative source, while allowing documented placeholder syntax where intentional.
caveats: The commit touches only source/elementdefinition-examples.html; there are no SVG, generated, or derived-file hunks to omit.
FHIR-26841 is relevant to the translation extension syntax but should not be treated as the sole page-level attribution for this source hunk.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-7173: Clarify NutritionOrder identifier V2 signpost
commits.summary: Clarified the current NutritionOrder.identifier comment so it directly states that Identifier.type can indicate an HL7 V2 placer or filler order identifier.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-7173 required NutritionOrder.identifier to signpost the HL7 V2 placer/filler order identifier distinction using Identifier.type. The current StructureDefinition comment is malformed and points readers to a ServiceRequest notes section that does not contain that promised explanation, so this targeted source correction should be kept.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-7173 was resolved as Persuasive with Modification and specifically required a NutritionOrder.identifier note that Identifier.type can indicate filler versus placer when needed, in response to a request to relate the element to HL7 V2 placer and filler orders. The current NutritionOrder.identifier comment only partially carries that application forward: it says "can be to indicate filler vs. placer" and sends readers to servicerequest.html#notes for further detail that is not present there. Because the comment is on the active NutritionOrder StructureDefinition element, it affects current generated element documentation and the distributed conformance resource; the matching Request mapping exception is the source surface that keeps the resource-specific comment synchronized with Request-pattern mapping review. The edit is necessary to complete the original clarification because it directly supplies the missing readable HL7 V2 placer/filler signpost in the affected element comment and removes the misleading cross-reference, without broadening the Jira into a structural or cross-resource policy change.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition comment for NutritionOrder.identifier is an authoritative element comment that is rendered in the current specification and included in generated conformance content. The mapping-exception XML is not a diagram or generated-only artifact here; it records the resource-specific divergence from the Request pattern so pattern-mapping QA stays aligned with the authoritative element wording.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix. No subset needs to be dropped; any broader requester/placer versus performer/filler policy discussion should be handled separately if OO wants to revisit it.

jira_evidence.explanation: The published resolution says to use the existing V2 mappings and add a note on NutritionOrder.identifier that Identifier.type can indicate filler versus placer if needed. That directly justifies replacing the malformed current comment and stale ServiceRequest-notes pointer with a clear HL7 V2 placer/filler order identifier statement.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-26565: Allow empty Parameters through ele-1
commits.summary: Restored the empty Parameters exception to the active ele-1/global-1 source so generated Schematron no longer rejects an otherwise empty Parameters resource.

The current active source in source/datatypes/element.xml still had the generic ele-1 wording, FHIRPath, and XPath without the Parameters exception, even though Parameters.parameter is 0..* and an empty Parameters resource is structurally possible. That source feeds the common Element invariant definition and generated Schematron/validation behavior, so the omission can make current generated validation artifacts contradict the approved rule. Adding the Parameters exception in exactly those three invariant fields is necessary to complete the approved correction while preserving the later FHIR-43103 'or both' wording clarification.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/datatypes/element.xml is an authoritative datatype spreadsheet source for the common Element invariant. The changed human text affects rendered invariant wording, the FHIRPath expression affects conformance/validation semantics, and the XPath affects generated Schematron so empty Parameters resources are no longer rejected by the global element rule.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix and regenerate any derived outputs through the normal build rather than hand-editing generated artifacts.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core Parameters and resolved to make a technical correction because generated Schematron global-1 did not allow an empty Parameters resource. That directly requires an exception in the common ele-1/global-1 source used to generate the FHIRPath and Schematron behavior.

This later Published issue listed the same R4B ele-1 changes: add 'or $this is Parameters', add 'unless an empty Parameters resource', and add '|self::f:Parameters', and said to make sure the correction was also applied in R5.
This later Applied issue clarified the ele-1 human wording to include 'or both'. The proposed edit preserves that clarification while adding the older Parameters exception.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-26431: Generalize CapabilityStatement scope wording

The authoritative Observation element and search parameter now reflect that model, but the active Security and Privacy module still told readers that Observation.context could hold Encounter or EpisodeOfCare, so the narrative incompletely applied the resolved model. commits.author: Josh Mandel

commits.summary: Aligned the active Identifier datatype spreadsheet detail with the applied RFC3986 fallback rule.

triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an editor-owned datatype spreadsheet, not a generated hard-avoid artifact. Its Identifier.value comment is used for current datatype definitions and conformance-facing generated output, so leaving the stale text would continue to publish an element-level statement that conflicts with the accepted Identifier guidance allowing assigned identifier systems for URI-expressible globally unique values.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix. No subset should be dropped; the single changed hunk is the authoritative Identifier.value detail that needs to match the accepted assigned-system/fallback rule.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution added the no-assigned-system qualifier to the Identifier guidance for globally unique URI values, responding to the request that more specific identifier systems such as urn:dicom:uid not be displaced by urn:ietf:rfc:3986. The DICOM UID identifier-type issue exposed the ambiguity that led to FHIR-19602 and documents why a specific identifier system can be needed for DICOM UIDs, but it does not by itself require this Identifier.value comment change.

caveats: The later FHIR-45479 wording is the closest match to the exact replacement text, but FHIR-19602 is still a direct attribution because it introduced the no-assigned-system qualification that the stale spreadsheet comment omitted.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-51725: Clarify extension references in compartments
commits.summary: Clarified the active CompartmentDefinition note so extension-based references may make resources available through compartment-based retrieval without implying formal compartment membership unless a CompartmentDefinition search parameter identifies the relationship.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application for the CompartmentDefinition narrative, with mixed attribution: FHIR-5816 explains why extension-reference discretion is documented, while the later FHIR-51725 decision requires the wording to avoid implying formal compartment membership. The edit updates an active rendered notes file and should be kept as a narrow source correction.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-51725 resolved concrete compartment semantics: listed resources with one or more CompartmentDefinition.resource.param elements are part of the compartment, listed resources without .param are outside it, and non-member resources may still be returned through _include or local convention in compartment-based retrieval operations. The existing CompartmentDefinition notes still carried the FHIR-5816 sentence saying servers may "include resources in a compartment" when the relevant reference is in an extension, which conflicts with the later search-parameter-based membership rule by implying that an extension reference alone can establish formal compartment membership. The changed file is the active CompartmentDefinition notes source, so the stale wording affects rendered explanatory specification text for compartment semantics. Rewording the sentence to distinguish availability through retrieval operations from formal membership is necessary to complete the later Jira application while preserving the original FHIR-5816 discretion guidance.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The change affects source/compartmentdefinition/compartmentdefinition-notes.xml, an active narrative source for the CompartmentDefinition resource. It corrects reader-visible compartment semantics by aligning the extension-reference note with the current rule that formal compartment membership depends on CompartmentDefinition search parameters, while still allowing server discretion for retrieval availability.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source change, but treat FHIR-51725 as the decisive Jira basis for the revised membership wording and FHIR-5816 as historical context for keeping extension-reference discretion guidance.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied resolution specifically states that resources with .param elements are part of a compartment, resources without .param are outside it, and non-members may still be returned by _include or local convention. That directly requires replacing wording that says extension references can cause resources to be included in a compartment with wording about retrieval availability unless a search parameter identifies the relationship.

The Published/Persuasive DSTU1 issue requested documentation that servers decide how to handle compartment relationships when the reference is carried by an extension, and it was historically applied as the note now being revised. It supports retaining the discretion guidance but does not by itself require the newer formal-membership distinction.

caveats: The commit changes only an editor-owned narrative XML source file; no generated, derived, or hard-avoid files are included.
The issue label FHIR-5816 is incomplete attribution because the source text became stale only after the later FHIR-51725 compartment-membership decision.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-2973: Fix Observation BMD UCUM unit code
commits.summary: Corrected the active Observation BMD example so the UCUM-coded Quantity uses g/cm2 instead of the erroneous g/cm-2.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-2973 specifically called out a sample value using `g/cm-2` as a UCUM code, and the active BMD Observation example still carries that exact invalid coded unit. The commit is a narrow authoritative example-source correction from `g/cm-2` to the UCUM expression `g/cm2`.
triage.category_rationale: Resolution: FHIR-2973 was resolved as a persuasive-with-modification OO correction to fix coding errors in examples, and its request text specifically identified a `g/cm-2` value claiming to be a UCUM code as one of the errors to fix. Missed application: although earlier work corrected other example coding issues from that ticket, `source/observation/observation-example-bmd.xml` still has `valueQuantity.system` set to UCUM with `valueQuantity.code` set to `g/cm-2`. Current spec impact: this is an editor-owned Observation example linked from the Observation example list and narrative pages, so the coded Quantity unit is rendered/distributed as example content and is subject to UCUM-code correctness. Necessity: changing only the code to `g/cm2` completes the specific UCUM-code correction while preserving the human display unit `g/cm²`; it is not generated collateral or optional consistency cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an active Observation example source, not a generated or layout-only artifact. The stale value affects the current example's machine-readable Quantity.code and can mislead readers or validation/QA consumers about the correct UCUM expression for grams per square centimeter.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix. No subset split is needed because the commit touches only the authoritative Observation example XML.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolved issue requested correction of example coding errors and explicitly named a `g/cm-2` value claiming to be a UCUM code; that resolution directly requires correcting the remaining active example instance using that UCUM-code error.

This later Observation issue quoted the DXA/BMD Observation example with the same `g/cm-2` code while discussing imaging results as Observations, tying the stale string to the current BMD Observation example lineage. It does not itself require the unit-code correction.
This later Quantity issue reinforces that UCUM strings in Quantity.code are checked as codes rather than display text, but it is not the responsible decision for this example correction.

caveats: The BMD example appears to have been introduced after an earlier partial application of FHIR-2973, so this is best understood as completing or preserving the same resolved correction on the current authoritative example surface.
